topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Biological Definition and Modeling of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a failure of normal cellular differentiation driven by accumulated genetic alterations and discuss the challenges of modeling tissue architecture in vitro.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical and histological differences between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on tissue invasion, metastasis, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor Classification and Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the standard rules and common exceptions used to name benign and malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the physiological mechanisms by which local tumor growth and distant metastases cause systemic illness and death.

topics.label: Neoplastic Incidence Across Tissues and Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the epidemiological patterns of tumor incidence across human tissues and throughout multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Practice of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, clinical execution, and diagnostic efficacy of screening modalities across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding section wraps up the lecture and refers students back to the initial learning outcomes.
